summary: Backend-only E2E testing of NOG Fase 1 (cupo per AUTHORIZATION/No. SPS) via REST, using an isolated TEST_ unit with 3 TEST NOGs (cantidad 50/2/10). All data was cleaned up afterwards, and a check confirmed 0 leftover units, NOGs, patients or evaluations. 16 tests ran: 13 passed, 3 failed. Cupo consumption works. A patient with 2 orders on the same NOG and different SPS uses 2 cupos, and each acreditación stores no_sps. Extra consultations under an existing SPS do not deduct. 1 SPS plus 3 evaluations uses 1 cupo. With no SPS, 2 evaluations use 1 cupo (legacy). An evaluation with a new SPS uses 1 cupo once. A legacy acreditación without SPS blocks new SPS. PUT on the patient is idempotent, and adding or removing an SPS adds or frees 1 cupo. The NOG counter matches the active acreditaciones. The 100% block works: 3 SPS on a cantidad-2 NOG gives acreditados=2, estado completado, with no overdraw. The 90% warning works: 9/10 gives por_completarse, and /nogs/alertas lists both the 90% and the 100% NOG. Over a full date range, production shows one row per (patient, SPS), and the row date is the earliest consultation even when it was created later. igss.admin can access /produccion, /nogs/all and /nogs/alertas. FAILED: (1) the production listing is built only from evaluations inside the queried date range, so a follow-up under the same SPS shows up as a new row on its own day or month; (2) production lists authorizations that never used a cupo; (3) editing an unrelated patient field (phone) cancels a cupo that a new-SPS evaluation had used.

critical.issue: Grouping by authorization is applied only to the evaluations inside the queried date range (_build_produccion_rows q['fecha']). Repro: SPS-B1 first consultation on 2025-11-10, follow-up on 2025-11-12. GET ?fecha=2025-11-12 returns a row for SPS-B1 dated 2025-11-12. With daily filters (the default is today) or monthly ranges that cross the first consultation, the same authorization appears again as a new production/billing line, which breaks the rule 'dos consultas bajo el mismo No. SPS no generan dos filas'.

An acreditación created by an evaluation with a new SPS (origen='evaluacion', SPS not in patient.igss_ordenes) is cancelled with motivo reasignacion_nog on ANY patient PUT, even a phone-only change. Repro: patient with order SPS-B1, evaluation with igss_no_sps SPS-B2 (acreditados +1), then PUT {phone} -> acreditados -1. The cupo is freed while the production row stays.

minor.issue: Production is evaluation-driven and ignores acreditaciones. Authorizations that did NOT use a cupo still show as billable rows, for example: an evaluation with a new SPS blocked by a legacy no-SPS acreditación (the comodín), or an evaluation on a NOG that is already at 100% (SPS-K9 on the full NOG). This is inconsistent with 'la unidad que descuenta cupo y aparece en producción es la autorización'. Confirm whether it is intended.
The group key is (paciente_id, ('sps', no_sps)) and does not include the NOG number, so the same SPS on two different NOGs of one patient would merge into one row. This is an edge case.
Mixed orders on the same NOG (one with SPS, one without) depend on the iteration order of set(pares): the '' order blocks or is blocked depending on order, so the result is non-deterministic.

This still calls _crear_acreditacion without no_sps, so retroactive or recalculated acreditaciones are legacy wildcards (no SPS). They then block all further SPS for that patient on that NOG, so a patient with 2 SPS synced retroactively uses only 1 cupo.
igss_no_sps shows the FIRST matching order's SPS for every acreditación of that NOG, not the acreditación's own no_sps. A patient with SPS-A1 and SPS-A2 shows SPS-A1 twice. It should use a['no_sps'].

Manual apply creates an acreditación without SPS (a wildcard) and returns 'duplicada' whenever the patient already has any acreditación on the NOG, so you cannot manually apply a second authorization.

action_items: In _build_produccion_rows: for each (paciente, SPS/NOG) group, check whether an evaluation of the same authorization exists BEFORE the range start (or the 'fecha' filter). If one exists, drop the group, or always compute the first-consultation date globally and include the row only if that date falls in the range.

In _reconciliar_nog_paciente: do not cancel origen='evaluacion' acreditaciones whose SPS comes from a real evaluation. Either keep them as targets (union of order SPS and evaluated SPS), or add the new SPS to patient.igss_ordenes when the evaluation uses it.
Decide whether production should only list authorizations with an active acreditación (or flag them as 'sin cupo'), so billing stays consistent with cupo.
In listar_pacientes_nog and the Excel export: show the acreditación's own no_sps.
In _sincronizar_acreditaciones: pass the SPS of each order (iterate the patient's orders) so retroactive sync does not create wildcards.
critical_code_review_comments: igss_nogs.py is 1432 lines and should be split (catalog/acreditaciones, mantenimiento, produccion, excel).
_order_key should include the NOG number: ('sps', numero, sps).
The evaluation hook in evaluaciones.py swallows all exceptions (except: pass), so acreditación failures are silent. At least log them.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest /app/backend/tests/test_nog_por_autorizacion.py. It is self-contained: it creates its own unit and NOGs and cleans up via pymongo on test_database. Evaluations are posted to /api/evaluaciones with motivo_consulta as clinical content. Patient creation itself uses cupo (reconcile at POST /patients). The 3 failing tests encode the expected behaviour for the reported bugs.
rca of the issue: (1) _build_produccion_rows queries evaluaciones_oftalmologicas filtered by fecha, desde or hasta, then groups only that subset. The 'primera consulta' is the first one inside the window, not the first one for the authorization. (2) _reconciliar_nog_paciente builds target_keys only from patient.igss_ordenes. An acreditación from _acreditar_evaluacion with an evaluation-only SPS matches no target and is not 'manual', so it is cancelled (motivo reasignacion_nog) on every PUT /patients/{id}.
